title: ClientCommand
description: A command from a UI client to the runtime.

oneOf.description: Read local durable sources; never starts their runtimes.

Manage user-global scheduled automation.

The schedule store remains the single authority; this command is the structured adapter every client uses, so no client parses human-readable CLI output back into state. The answer is [`crate::RuntimeEvent::ScheduleManaged`] carrying the same `query_id`.

Ask the runtime for one best-effort prediction of the user's next prompt. The request is advisory UI chrome: it starts no task, persists no message, and may produce no event when there is insufficient context.
Generate a one-shot recap after the UI has observed a post-turn idle window. The runtime may decline when the conversation is too short.
Submit a user message; the runtime drives a turn in the given session.

Steer the turn that is already running: the text is injected at the top of the next round instead of waiting for the turn to end. This is the default meaning of Enter while a turn runs.

The runtime persists the text before it acknowledges the command. A turn that ends before the next round still delivers it as a new turn, so it is never silently dropped. A correction like "actually use the other module" is worthless once the work is finished, which is why it joins the running turn rather than a later one.

When no turn is running the runtime starts one with the same text, so the busy/idle race in the client cannot lose the message.

`message_id` is the client's stable identity for this input. The runtime echoes it in `InputAdmitted` and every later state event, so a retry cannot create a second row and a client can update the exact row it drew. Legacy clients omit it; the runtime generates one.
Run an explicit goal task. Unlike ordinary chat messages, this enables goal-mode completion (`update_goal`) in the agent loop.

require_new_turn.description: Refuse to join a turn another client is already running instead of steering into it. An unattended delivery must own the turn it starts, so its terminal can be attributed to that delivery alone. Defaulted for wire compatibility with clients that predate it.

oneOf.description:
Continue the session's interrupted logical task through the runtime's existing resume path, instead of starting a fresh turn.

This is an EXPLICIT client command: the user chose to resume, so the client does not need to classify their words. The runtime remains the authority on whether a resumable task actually exists. When none does, the runtime falls back to the ordinary submit path, so a `ResumeTask` is never lost — it is either a resume or a normal message.

`content` is the user's own text, preserved alongside the original objective and added to it, never replacing it.

Import a file as an attachment; the runtime processes and stores it.

`name` overrides the display name that would otherwise come from the file name. A terminal that answers Cmd+V on an image by writing a scratch file and pasting its path knows the file name is its own bookkeeping (`clipboard-2026-09-16-215212-CE7C9522.png`) and not something the user chose — only the client that made the gesture knows that, so only it can say so.
Import an attachment from immutable base64-encoded bytes already read by a trusted client. This avoids reopening an ambient path after a security-sensitive upload or file-picker validation.
Import an image from the system clipboard (spec §38.1).

Retire this runtime once its current work has settled.

One mechanism covers both cases the caller cares about: an idle runtime drains instantly and exits, a busy one stops taking new work and exits when the work it already owns is done. The caller never polls for idleness and never kills anything — the runtime owns the drain, because only it knows what "still working" means.

End this runtime NOW for a generation handover, cancelling the main turns it still owns instead of waiting for them to reach a terminal.

The explicit, user-chosen escape from a handover whose drain cannot finish — a turn that will never terminate on its own. Distinct from `Quit`: this is a version handover, not a user shutdown, so it never kills background work. The caller must have settled those first; the runtime keeps waiting for them if any remain.

Re-read every configured source and apply what can be applied without a restart (the `/reload` command).

Session-less by design: configuration is runtime-wide, and the answer belongs to the requester, not to one conversation. The runtime keeps executing turns on the generation they started with; only later turns see the new one.

Cooperatively cancel the running turn (graceful; resumable).

This is the only turn cancel the protocol offers: it asks the runtime to stop the current work window and settle the turn as resumable `interrupted`. Older 1.x clients may still put `force_cancel_current_turn` on the wire; that payload is accepted as this same command and produces the same terminal. There is no separate force-cancel capability to escalate to, so the protocol must not imply one.

Cancel the logical task, not just the running turn.

Distinct from [`Self::CancelCurrentTurn`]: that interrupts the current work window and leaves the task resumable, while this is the user saying the task itself is over. The runtime commits a terminal `cancelled` outcome, settles the goal, and refuses a later continuation — a `继续` must not silently reopen it.
Cancel ONE running delegated child of the session's turn. The child settles as cancelled; its parent turn keeps running.
Stop ONE running tool call of the session's turn (for a command, its whole process tree). The call settles with its own stop outcome; the turn keeps running. Rejected when no such call is executing.

Acknowledge the session's crash window: close every tool call that started but never recorded an outcome with an explicit "outcome unknown, not replayed" marker, so the next turn may run.

This is the interactive counterpart of `run --resume --confirm-recovery`. It asserts only that the user inspected the workspace; it never turns an unknown result into success, never replays a call, and is refused while a turn is executing. The runtime answers with [`crate::RuntimeEvent::CrashWindowAcknowledged`] and a fresh snapshot.
Resolve a pending permission request .
Answer a pending clarification (spec §35). An empty answer means "skip".

session_id.description: The session that owns the request. A live waiter is found by request id alone; the session is what lets a runtime with no in-memory waiter — a restarted daemon — settle the durable request and continue the goal. Older clients omit it and can answer only a live waiter.

oneOf.description: Switch the model used for subsequent turns .

The user's explicit "use this model from now on": switch the active session's model AND persist it as the user's default model for future sessions.

Distinct from [`Self::SelectModel`] on purpose. Only this command carries the authority to rewrite the user's persisted configuration, because only an explicit user action does. Runtime fallbacks, provider failover, retries, temporary CLI/session overrides and internal routing MUST use [`Self::SelectModel`] (session-scoped) and never touch the default.
Switch the execution mode used for subsequent turns .

Set or clear this session's Thinking Level.

`Some(level)` sets an explicit level for this session — including `auto`, which is a choice ("do not override") and NOT the same as clearing one. `None` clears the override, so the session goes back to the level configured for the model or globally.

The stored value is always CodeLeveler's canonical level. What that becomes on the wire is resolved per request from the model's declared capability, so switching models re-resolves instead of carrying one model's parameter to another.
Set collaboration (`chat | plan | goal`). `work_profile` is a deprecated compatibility field accepted from old clients and ignored by the runtime.
Confirm a collaboration-plan proposal and auto-enter goal mode (K24).

content.description: Optional plan body; empty uses the last assistant proposal text.

oneOf.description: Recompute and return the working-tree diff.

query_id.description: Correlates the response to the requesting client. Automatic diff updates remain uncorrelated broadcasts.

oneOf.description: Summarize and compact the conversation history (spec §28, §53).
Start a fresh conversation: drop the session's stored message history so the next turn carries no prior context (a real "new chat", not a screen clear).
Ask for the list of stored sessions (spec §52).
Ask for the session list and route the response only to the requesting session's event stream.

List the locally stored sessions of another coding agent, newest first. Read-only: discovery never opens a picker entry into CodeLeveler, and the answer is a [`crate::RuntimeEvent::ForeignSessionList`] routed to the requesting session.
Import one foreign session by exact native id and continue its work in a NEW CodeLeveler session. The source file is read, never modified.

Start a FRESH session and switch the requester's view to it, leaving the current one intact in the session list.

This is what `/clear` does. Wiping the current session in place would be destructive and unrecoverable (it takes the checkpoints with it), which is why that shape needed a confirmation; starting a new session loses nothing, so it needs none.
Open a stored session, loading its transcript into the view.
Open a stored session on behalf of another currently displayed session. The switch event is delivered to the requester before the client moves its subscription to the target.
Delete a stored session.
Delete a stored session and route the refreshed list to the requester.
Rename a stored session (overwrite its goal/title text).
Archive a stored session: it keeps its transcript but leaves the default session list.
Fork a stored session: create a new session with a copy of the transcript, so an alternative direction can be explored without touching the original.
Restore the conversation to a checkpoint (spec §68).

Side question (`/btw`): single-turn answer using current session context, without tools and without appending to the transcript store. Run an explicit user shell command (`!command`) in the session's repository. USER-ORIGINATED DIRECT EXECUTION: never reaches the model, the agent loop, or the tool registry. `command` is the raw shell string after the `!` prefix.

Move exactly one running foreground user shell to the background. This is an ownership transfer, not a re-run: the runtime keeps the same process and execution identity. Idempotent; it never spawns a second process.
Cancel exactly one user shell execution. Deliberately separate from `CancelCurrentTurn`: a user shell is not an agent turn, and the id match ensures a stale cancel can never kill a newer execution.

Stop one background task the runtime is still running. The registry signals the process tree through its own lifecycle; the task settles as killed. Deliberately separate from `CancelCurrentTurn` and `CancelUserShell`: a background task outlives the turn that started it, and stopping it must not stop the turn.
Stop the in-flight `/btw` side answer for a session. Deliberately separate from `CancelCurrentTurn`: a side thread's answer has its own lifecycle, and stopping it must never stop the main turn.
Read-only observatory query. Does not mutate runtime, tools, or verification. Results arrive as [`crate::RuntimeEvent::ObservabilityLoaded`].

after.description: Events at/after the center (capped by the runtime).

before.description: Events strictly before the center (capped by the runtime).

center_seq.description: Sequence to center the event window on. `None` = latest durable seq.

query_id.description: Correlation token for [`crate::RuntimeEvent::ObservabilityLoaded`]. Distinct from envelope `command_id` (delivery idempotency): this names the query so a client can ignore another client's (or its own stale) observatory response. Absent on protocol 1.5 peers. Not a session identity.

oneOf.description: Read-only context-accounting query. Does not mutate the runtime or the conversation. Answers with [`crate::RuntimeEvent::ContextLoaded`].

Read-only usage query over the runtime's durable model-call ledger.

Read-only in the strictest sense: it opens no turn, sends no provider request, and mutates nothing. Answers with [`crate::RuntimeEvent::UsageLoaded`]. A client may issue it while a turn runs; the numbers come from rows that already settled.

scope.description: Which window to aggregate. The runtime resolves it into an explicit range and echoes that range back.

utc_offset_minutes.description: The caller's UTC offset in minutes, so `today`/`last 7 days`/ `last 30 days` are the caller's own calendar days instead of the runtime host's. Range is validated by the runtime (`-1440..=1440`).

oneOf.description: Read-only memory status: the two scope manifests' counters and the files a page may list. Answers with [`crate::RuntimeEvent::MemoryLoaded`]. Opens no model turn and mutates nothing.
Load one memory file for the preview pane. The runtime bounds the path to the named scope and caps the payload. Answers with [`crate::RuntimeEvent::MemoryFileLoaded`].

path.description: Scope-relative path exactly as [`crate::UiMemoryFile::path`] listed it.

oneOf.description: Store a user-authored note in the global memory scope. A typed management action: it creates no agent turn and reaches no model. Answers with [`crate::RuntimeEvent::MemoryActionFinished`].
Run one Dream pass now. `batch = false` is the normal consolidation; `batch = true` is the read-then-edit Batch Dream. Both answer with [`crate::RuntimeEvent::MemoryActionFinished`] once settled.
Promote observations captured under RecordOnly/Shadow into the visible manifest. Idempotent. Answers with [`crate::RuntimeEvent::MemoryActionFinished`].

Turn cross-session memory on or off for one session.

The configured `[memory].rollout` stays the authority: this can only pause a rollout that is already on, and refuses to promote a configuration that says `off`. The change is session-scoped and lasts for this process; a new session starts from the configuration again. Answers with [`crate::RuntimeEvent::MemoryActionFinished`].

Forget exactly the file the user inspected. The expected content hash binds the tombstone to those bytes; a changed file is refused rather than silently deleted. Answers with [`crate::RuntimeEvent::MemoryActionFinished`].

Load one child's findings for the Contribution Inspector.

A query, not a subscription: findings live in the ledger, and pushing them through the event stream would duplicate the record and re-grow the payloads the event pipeline was trimmed of. The client asks when the user opens a detail view.

query_id.description: Correlation token for [`crate::RuntimeEvent::ChildContributionLoaded`], so a client ignores another client's — or its own stale — response.

oneOf.description:
Cut a durable goal checkpoint for the session's current goal and surface it as a Recap (long-goal P3, `/recap`).

This is NOT "summarize the visible transcript": the runtime projects authoritative facts (event log, evidence ledger, goal row) into a persisted GoalCheckpoint and answers with [`crate::RuntimeEvent::GoalRecapCreated`]. Idempotent at the same event boundary — a transport retry returns the same checkpoint.

List goals that still owe work (long-goal P2).

Read-only, and there is deliberately no companion command that continues one: resume is a policy this runtime has not decided, and a protocol that can only report is a protocol that cannot accidentally restart somebody's half-finished mutation.

The session's past turns as clients saw them live: its durable event log projected through the same client projection, with the user's messages in place. Answered by [`crate::RuntimeEvent::SessionHistoryLoaded`].
List the agent definitions the session's project resolves. Answered by [`crate::RuntimeEvent::AgentsLoaded`].
One agent with its full definition. Answered by [`crate::RuntimeEvent::AgentLoaded`].
Write a new agent definition. The user's own command is the authorization; the runtime validates and writes atomically, and answers with [`crate::RuntimeEvent::AgentMutated`].
Replace an existing agent definition in `scope`.
Delete an agent definition from `scope`. Running children keep theirs.
The runtime owner is shutting down; all work should stop. Disconnecting an individual UI client must not issue this command.

ApprovalId.description: Identifies a pending permission approval request.

AttachmentId.description: Identifies a pending or sent attachment.

AttachmentRef.description: A reference to a processed, stored attachment (spec §39). Carries only metadata; the bytes are addressed by `sha256` in the media store.

sha256.description: Content-address of the processed bytes in the media store.

CommandId.description: Identifies a client command, used as an idempotency key: a command may be delivered more than once (at-least-once), so the same id must not run the action twice.

MessageId.description:
Identifies a single assistant/user message in the transcript.

A protocol-level id (the runtime persists messages as an ordered log, not by id); it lets streaming deltas target the right in-flight message.

ModelRef.description: A provider + model pair. The rest of the system routes on this, never on a bare model-name string.

RestartReason.description:
Why a runtime is being asked to retire.

Typed rather than a string because the updater will reuse this exact lifecycle: install an artifact, ask the running runtime to retire, verify the replacement's identity. Only the reason differs.

oneOf.description: The connecting client is a different build than this runtime.
The connecting client sees a different effective configuration source generation than the running daemon loaded at boot.
A newer artifact is installed and waiting to take over. Reserved for the updater; nothing sends it yet.

An operator asked this project's runtime to restart (the Web project action, or any client acting on a person's explicit request).

Distinct from the generation reasons on purpose: `BuildMismatch` and `ConfigChanged` describe WHY a new generation is wanted, and reporting either for a plain operator restart would be a lie in the health a waiting client reads.

ScheduleActionWire.description: The declared work of a schedule, in wire form.

ScheduleDraft.description: The complete declaration a create request carries.

allow_external_side_effects.description: The grant also covers actions with external side effects.

grant_unattended.description: The user explicitly asked for unattended execution.

ScheduleFilter.description: Which definitions a client wants to see.

oneOf.description: Anything a person must act on: waiting approval, blocked, unknown or failed in the latest attempt.
The latest run is `failed`, `unknown` or `blocked`.

SchedulePatch.description: A partial replacement of an existing definition. Every absent field keeps its stored value; an empty `model` clears the model. `expected_revision` on the request is the optimistic-concurrency guard.

ScheduleRequest.description: One structured management request from a client.

expected_revision.description: The revision the client last observed. A mismatch is refused rather than overwriting a newer definition.

oneOf.description: The background-scheduler picture: OS registration, counts, next slot.

ScheduleTriggerWire.description: A trigger rule in the vocabulary a user can actually choose.

oneOf.description: One RFC3339 instant.
A fixed interval in seconds, anchored at `anchor` (default now).
One local wall-clock time per day.
Local wall-clock time on selected weekdays (`mon`, `mon-fri`, ...).
Five-field cron expression.

SessionId.description: Identifies a single agent session (one user goal end to end).

ThinkingLevel.description:
How hard the user wants the model to think, in CodeLeveler's own words.

The order is the product contract: weakest → strongest, with `Auto` first because "no override" precedes explicit intensity choices.

oneOf.description: No override. CodeLeveler does not specify reasoning intensity; the provider's own default applies.
Ask the route to disable extra thinking, where it can be asked.
The strongest level this model declares — not a fixed setting.

ToolCallId.description: Identifies a tool call. Must be stable across streaming reassembly.

UiAgentCapability.description: The runtime capability class an agent runs under.

UiAgentDraft.description: A definition a client asks the runtime to write.

UiAgentScope.description: Where a client may write a definition.

UiForeignTool.description: The agent whose local session store is read.

oneOf.description: Anthropic Claude Code.
OpenAI Codex.

UiUsageScope.description:
The window a usage report covers.

The runtime — not the client — resolves a scope into an explicit `[from, to)` range and echoes it in the report, so two surfaces showing the same scope can never disagree about its boundary.

oneOf.description: The session's latest turn (the running one, else the last one).
Everything the current session ever spent.
The caller's local calendar day.
The caller's local day six days ago through now.
The caller's local day twenty-nine days ago through now.
Every durable call this runtime's ledger holds.

UserShellId.description: Identifies one user-originated shell execution (`!command`) — a session-scoped direct host execution. Deliberately NOT a [`ToolCallId`]: a user shell is not an agent tool call and never enters the model conversation.
